doc_locations.cited: p.6 §7.1 'One or more refunds succeeded against a captured or succeeded payment.'
p.19 §26.1 FR-2 'Randomised event sequences ... never produce a transition outside Section 7.2'

findings.note: Correct against p.6 §7.2. There is no PARTIALLY_REFUNDED self-transition, no CAPTURED self-transition for repeated partial captures, and no path from a refund state to SETTLED, even though §16.2 settles matched payments. A failed wallet payment or 3DS challenge from REQUIRES_ACTION may arguably route via AUTHORISING, and a REVIEW hold could sit in AUTHORISED, so those sub-points are weaker. The point that the FR-2 test is negative-only is a good insight.

findings.note: A material internal contradiction, established correctly from the design's own figures (3.8% retryable vs '<1% cascade'; a 2,500 ms timeout vs the 1,500 ms NFR-2). It also notes that the §26.2 test injects 3.8%. 'Every one of them triggers a cascade' slightly overstates: scheme limits or no remaining candidate can stop a cascade. The deadline-based budget refines the confirmed cascade policy rather than reversing it. The owner is named.

p.8 §9.3 'Keying by merchant_id keeps each merchant's records co-located, which the local secondary index on'

findings.note: The direction is right, but the finding is under-researched. AWS documents a per-partition limit of 1,000 WCU/s (not 10,000) and a 10 GB item-collection limit for tables with an LSI. The design's ~1,800+ WCU on one key (more with 4 KB items) therefore definitely exceeds the limit. This is a checkable public fact, yet the review defers it as 'unverified' and cites no AWS source. Hedging is calibrated but leaves the verdict weaker than the evidence allows. Severity is closer to critical.

external_sources.cited: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirements 3.2.1 / 3.3.2 ('usual reading' that SAD may not be kept after authorization)

findings.note: The reading is correct. In v4.0, 3.2.1 and 3.3.2 cover SAD stored before authorization completes, and 3.3.1.2 prohibits keeping the CVC after authorization. Retention until settlement or for incremental authorizations is therefore non-compliant. The review is honest that it did not consult the standard ('No external source was available'), even though the standard is public and the matter decisive. This is a research miss. 'Unlawful' misuses the term for a contractual standard. Reopening the CVC decision is justified, and a QSA check is a reasonable next step.

material_issues.issue: Redis fast-path key idem:resp:{idempotency_key} omits merchant_id, and a cache hit returns before any body-hash check. This contradicts P3 and FR-5 (422 rule), and merchants' order-number keys make cross-merchant collisions likely.
The Fraud Hook detokenises the PAN using the Card Adapter role and sends it to FRV-1, yet §12.2 declares the Fraud Hook out of CDE scope. This contradicts P2, §12.1 and NFR-5.

The CVC is retained after authorization (until settlement or 72 h, and for incremental auths). This rests on a misreading of PCI DSS v4.0 3.2.1/3.3.2, which do not permit SAD retention after authorization.
NFR-4's zero RPO on region loss is impossible with asynchronous Aurora Global replication; idempotency stores are also recreated empty.
The latency budget claims <1% of payments cascade, but 3.8% are retryable, and the 2,500 ms timeout alone exceeds the 1,500 ms NFR-2.
A single CloudHSM in one AZ with no DEK caching is a SPOF for all card traffic. The 1,500 TPS trigger for a second HSM never fires (about 1,100 card TPS at peak).
The DynamoDB per-partition limit is wrongly stated as 10,000 WCU/s (AWS: 1,000). WCU are under-counted for 4 KB items, and the LSI imposes a 10 GB item-collection limit on one hot merchant key.

The NFR-8 08:00 SGT report deadline is unreachable: the ACQ-TH1 file arrives at 06:30 ICT (07:30 SGT), and match plus reports take 60 min at 2025 volume (about 08:30). There is also no late-file handling.

Money representation: integer minor units, versioned ISO 4217 exponents, adapter conversion that rejects rounding, single half-to-even fee rounding.
Webhook delivery: per-endpoint secrets, timestamped HMAC, bounded retry plus DLQ, per-endpoint isolation, DNS-pinned SSRF protection.

material_issues.issue: The Redis idempotency fast-path key idem:resp:{idempotency_key} has no merchant_id and no request-hash check. This contradicts P3 and FR-5, and §9.1 accepts order numbers as keys, so collisions between merchants are likely.
The Fraud Hook detokenises PAN using the Card Adapter role and sends it to FRV-1, yet §12.2 lists the Fraud Hook as out of CDE scope. This contradicts P2, §12.1 and NFR-5.

The CVC is kept until settlement or 72 h and reused for cascades and incremental authorizations. This rests on a misreading of PCI DSS v4.0 3.2.1/3.3.2, which do not allow keeping SAD after authorization.
NFR-4 requires zero RPO on loss of a region, but Aurora Global Database replication is asynchronous. Idempotency state is not replicated across regions.

The latency budget assumes fewer than 1% of payments cascade, but 3.8% of attempts are retryable. A 2,500 ms timeout cascade alone exceeds the 1,500 ms NFR-2 target, which explicitly includes cascades.
A single CloudHSM in one AZ, with no DEK caching, is a single point of failure for every card authorization. The 1,500 TPS trigger for a second HSM never fires at about 1,100 card TPS.

NFR-8 cannot be met. The ACQ-TH1 file arrives at 06:30 ICT (07:30 SGT); adding the 45 + 15 minute run gives about 08:30 SGT, after the 08:00 SGT deadline, even at 2025 volume.
